status: best guess; a candidate list of protected objects of the working law with labels checked on operators. No particle is identified and no mass is given.

working_law.carrier: pinned twelve-port source: 12 ports, 30 seams, 20 faces, 60 rotations, cover of order 120
working_law.local_state: port x five-level code x two-state record x sixty addresses (7,200), thirty link bits
programs: repair-law/candidates/CF1.md section 8 with the corrections of sections 11 and 12
working_law.scheduler: address reflection; sorted interior edges (joint program); three axes in alternating order (CF-1)

conventions.Q6: 3 n2 - 2 n3 = six times the hypercharge; the lifted public charge Q5 with the sign reversed
conventions.handedness_class: even occupation is called left (simulation chart); nothing supplies chirality
conventions.cover_irreps: of the cover of order 120: 1, 2, 2', 3, 3', 4, 4s, 5, 6; spinorial: 2, 2', 4s, 6; the code is 3 + 2'

corrections_stated_first: CF1.md section 12 and the coordinator's note say that 30 patterns have nonzero charge modulo 6. Exact count: 30 of 32 states have Q6 nonzero; 28 have Q6 nonzero modulo 6. The four singlets (0,0), (3,0), (0,2), (3,2) see no centre flux of any class (as in reports/CH.md).

Of the three flux rows of MAP.md only class 3 is an object of the working law: its Z2 face flux. Classes 1 and 5 reduce to it modulo 2; classes 2 and 4 are flat for its register. CF-1 version 1 carries a class label k per carrier as a static declared background only.
work/FAMILY/FAMILY.md uses 6Y = 2 n3 - 3 n2; MAP.md, the audit and the simulation chart use Q6 = 3 n2 - 2 n3. The two differ by conjugation of every name. This table uses Q6 = 3 n2 - 2 n3.

The native spinor of the carrier is the spinor doublet of the code. In the chart the same two states are the weak index. A pattern with n2 = 1 therefore has a native pointer or a weak doublet index, not both; patterns with n2 even have no native pointer.
